articles.title: PNG Chiefs unveil logo and jersey for first NRL season amid naming dispute with rival code
articles.summary: Design by artist Tabu includes face of a chief to represent ‘leadership’ NZ Rugby injunction over use of Chiefs moniker denied in high court. The PNG Chiefs have pushed ahead with the unveiling of their logo and jersey despite lingering legal issues with New Zealand Rugby over its rights to use the…
body: Pending the outcome of a dispute in New Zealand, the Chiefs will run on to an NRL field for the first time in two years in a black jersey with a white accented “V” and a chest adorned with gold cultural drawings by PNG artist Tabu, with an alternative version largely swapping the black for white.

The club is yet to designate either as the home design, but has formally adopted black, white and gold as its official colours. The palette echoes the colours in the Papua New Guinea flag of red, black, yellow and white that have traditionally been worn by its national sporting teams.
The Chiefs join Penrith, Wests, the Warriors and 2027 entrants Perth Bears as NRL clubs who regularly wear black.
A legal dispute between New Zealand Rugby and the NRL over the Chiefs trademark centres around the Super Rugby club Waikato Chiefs formed in 1996.

articles.title: Football regulator has ‘absolute power’ to force Manchester City sale if verdict upheld
articles.summary: IFR chair David Kogan insists regulator has power to act. City have appealed against Premier League’s charges. The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) will have “absolute power” to force Manchester City’s owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog’s…
body: Manchester City have been found guilty of circumventing Premier League rules by an independent commission, which found they set up “sham” commercial arrangements to inflate revenues or reduce costs by over £900m over a nine-season period.

They were also found to have made “concerted efforts” to “stop and frustrate” the Premier League’s investigation into those arrangements. City have lodged an appeal, claiming the verdict “contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”.

David Kogan, the chair of the IFR, told podcast The Rest Is Football it was premature to talk about any action his organisation might take while the appeal was ongoing. Kogan did confirm, though, that the IFR had “absolute power” to force a sale by the club’s ownership, if that was felt to be appropriate.

“We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety,” Kogan said. Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan replied: “No, no, no. We’ve got absolute power to do so.”

articles.title: No Haaland, no problem - can Foden be Man City's alternative goalscorer?
articles.summary: Phil Foden's magnificent man-of-the-match display in Manchester City's Champions League win against AEK Athens serves as a reminder of his talent and ability to influence games.
body: Phil Foden's magnificent man-of-the-match display in the Champions League against AEK Athens served as a reminder of the prodigious talent that the player still possesses.
After two disappointing seasons in which, by his own admission, he failed to hit the heights expected, there may be those who had forgotten what he can produce.

Being left out of the England squad for the World Cup last summer did not help, but he came into this season telling reporters he was looking forward to a "fresh start" under new manager Enzo Maresca.

Up until last weekend, that fresh start had been a slow burner with the low point of being sent off in the derby against Manchester United in September, before he sparked into life by netting against Ipswich on Saturday.

articles.title: Robinson sparks 23-0 run as Pistons stun Celtics in NBA season opener
articles.summary: Detroit erase 22-point deficit to beat Boston 121-113. Paul George scores 38 points on Celtics debut in defeat. Robinson scores 15 of his 21 points in fourth quarter. Duncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter as the Detroit Pistons reeled off 23 unanswered points to beat the…
body: Jalen Duren and Cade Cunningham scored 22 points apiece for the Pistons, who led the Eastern Conference with 60 wins last season.
Javonte Green came off the bench to score 19 points in 18 minutes, while Ausar Thompson added 11 points, 11 rebounds and five assists.

Paul George scored a game-high 38 points on his Celtics debut. Payton Pritchard and Derrick White scored 17 points apiece, but Jayson Tatum was held to 13 points on six-for-23 shooting, although he contributed 11 assists.
The Celtics led by 13 at halftime thanks to a second-quarter surge. Detroit held a 39-35 advantage early in the quarter before Boston reeled off 15 unanswered points.

articles.title: Champions League roundup: McTominay double leads Napoli past Bodø/Glimt
articles.summary: Midfielder scores for first time since heart surgery. Ten-man Atlético hang on for draw against Stuttgart. Scott McTominay scored his first two goals of the season to help Napoli beat Bodø/Glimt 4-3 and relieve pressure on the coach, Massimiliano Allegri.
body: Matteo Politano’s first-minute opener was cancelled out by Bodø’s Jens Petter Hauge. McTominay restored Napoli’s lead before the break only for Andreas Helmersen to again level for the Norwegian club.
The Scotland midfielder struck again on 71 minutes and Odin Bjørtuft’s late own goal secured the result. Bodø still managed an injury-time consolation from Sondre Brunstad Fet.
Atlético Madrid held on with 10 men for a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart, foiling the German underdogs’ bid to join Paris Saint-Germain and Liverpool at the top of the table on nine points.

Julián Alvarez’s goal for Atlético had cancelled out Jamie Leweling’s opener when the midfielder Morten Hjulmand made a reckless sliding tackle from behind on Angelo Stiller, resulting in a red card that left Atlético clinging on.

articles.title: GB men take fourth and must wait for LA28 Olympic spot
articles.summary: Great Britain just miss out on earning a spot at the 2028 Olympic Games at the first attempt, placing fourth in the men's team final at the Gymnastics World Championships.
body: Only the top three in Rotterdam were assured of early qualification for the Games in Los Angeles in two years' time, with defending champions Japan taking the gold medal ahead of Russia in second and China in third.
GB's next chance to qualify will be at the World Championships in Chengdu, China in 2027, where a top-nine finish will secure a place in LA.
Courtney Tulloch, Joe Fraser, Jake Jarman, Harry Hepworth and Reuben Ward qualified in second place for the final and finished with a total score of 247.395 on Tuesday.

The team were leading the standings after four of the six rotations, but they just fell short of staying in the medal places as Japan, Russia and China all improved in the closing stages. Japan took the step on the podium with a score of 251.928.

articles.title: Spurs Silver Dancers return to the dance floor after 8-year hiatus
articles.summary: Suddenly, it feels like 2014. The Spurs Silver Dancers returned to the court on Tuesday, October 20, ending an eight-year hiatus during San Antonio's season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder.
body: Fans have longed for this comeback for years, ever since Spurs Sports and Entertainment announced the Silver Dancers wouldn't return to the court because of a "lack of interest" ahead of the 2018-2019 season, according to past reporting from MySA.

At the time, the Spurs replaced the Silver Dancers with the Hype Squad, a co-ed dance squad that remains part of the organization. Ahead of the 2025-26 season, the team also formed the Spurs Jackals, a dedicated, high-energy supporter section created by Spurs star Victor Wembanyama. Both the Hype Squad and the Spurs Jackals are great additions to the fanbase, but nothing compares to the Silver Dancers.

The Spurs announced in June that the Silver Dancers would return for the 2026-27 season, shortly after the team's 2026 playoff run. The Silver Dancers trace their roots to the 1982-83 season, when the first squad debuted as the Quicksilver dance troupe at the old Hemisfair Arena. They predated the vaunted Spurs Coyote by half a season.
The San Antonio Spurs game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday, October 20, starts at 8:30 p.m. Central Time in San Antonio at the Frost Bank Center.

articles.title: Carrick wants more clean sheets to turn season around
articles.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick needs more clean sheets as he looks to change his team's fortunes, as they take on Como in the Champions League.
body: The question that prompted it in his pre-match news conference at a rain-lashed Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium in Como concerned his side's failure to keep clean sheets.
It was put to Carrick that it would help if United could manage some shutouts, and he was asked if he had figured out the problem.
United have kept the opposition out just once in 10 games this season, against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK last month.
"There's definitely parts of our game we have to improve to make things easier. I am fully aware of that," said Carrick, whose side take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs weren't just ready to make a statement on the court Tuesday night. They were also turning heads with their fashion choices. Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and Julian Champagnie showed off their personal styles as they arrived at…

Wembanyama took a more sophisticated approach, arriving in a blue suit paired with a light blue striped button-down shirt and black dress shoes. Although the designer has not been confirmed, the suit could be from Louis Vuitton, the French luxury fashion house for which Wembanyama serves as a brand ambassador.

Vassell went with a bold designer look, sporting a Bottega Veneta Blouson jacket paired with printed black pants. The Spurs guard accessorized with a gold cross necklace, a statement belt buckle and a large duffel bag.

Castle embraced a darker streetwear aesthetic, wearing an Enfants Riches Déprimés Madonne Assemblage Zip Up Hoodie in "Faded Black." Underneath, the Spurs guard sported a vintage Harley-Davidson "Live Hard, Ride Easy" graphic T-shirt. He completed the look with black pants and a statement belt buckle.

articles.title: Every celebrity that attended New York Knicks ring ceremony including Harry Styles
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are incredibly popular, but some of their fans might just be even more famous. Here’s a look at every celebrity present for the ring ceremony on opening night. The New York Knicks raised the banner for their 2026 NBA championship on Tuesday night.
body: The Knicks’ star-studded fanbase was a massive part of their run through the playoffs last season. It was as common to see the likes of Ben Stiller and Timothee Chalamet during games as it was seeing Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart. And ring night brought most of the celebs back to the building, with one notable exception.

There were more big names in attendance for this than probably ever before at Madison Square Garden. The first mention goes to the longest-serving and most passionate fans. Stiller, Tracy Morgan, Spike Lee, and Law & Order: SVU star Mariska Hargitay were all seen celebrating.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell was in attendance, as was Mark Shapiro. Mets owner Steve Cohen was spotted at the game, as was former presidential candidate Chris Christie. Some of music’s biggest names were there too. Fat Joe is a Knicks superfan, but Jon Bon Jovi was in attendance. Of course, Harry Styles’ presence also caught the people’s attention.

articles.title: NBA season tips off as Detroit stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Celtics
articles.summary: Detriot Pistons staged an epic 23-0 run in the fourth quarter as they overcame a 22-point deficit - the largest come-from-behind win against the Boston Celtics in the last 30 seasons - to seal a stunning 121-113 win.
body: Javonte Green scored 19 points after not playing in the first half and Cade Cunningham finished with 22 points and eight assists, helping the Pistons to victory as the NBA season tipped off in style on Tuesday.

Paul George scored 38 points, the most by a Celtic in his debut. The nine-time All-Star, in his 17th season, showed he's still got it in his first game with Boston since it acquired him from Philadelphia in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown.
Jayson Tatum, a six-time All-Star, was off his game, missing 17 of 23 shots and had 13 points and 11 assists.
His lack of hustle on defense allowed Green to take his time for a fifth 3-pointer that gave the Pistons a 13-point lead with 3:33 left.

articles.title: Every player from Arizona to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Ron Brewer
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the…
body: From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club.
For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from Arizona who has played for Brooklyn.

Our focus in this article is Ron Brewer. An alum of Northside high school and University of Arkansas-Fort Smith, Arkansas, he was picked up with the seventh overall selection of the 1978 NBA Draft by the Portland Trail Blazers.

The Fort Smith, Arkansas native played the first 3 seasons of his pro career with Portland. He also played for the San Antonio Spurs, Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors and Spurs again before he signed with the (then) New Jersey (now, Brooklyn) Nets in 1985. His stay with the team lasted until he signed with the Chicago Bulls that fall.

articles.title: Hat-trick hero Foden shines as Man City thrash AEK Athens
articles.summary: Phil Foden bagged a hat-trick as dominant Manchester City cruised to a 5-1 win over AEK Athens to claim their second Champions League victory of the campaign.
body: Foden had waited 10 months for a goal before four arrived in back-to-back outings, adding to his strike against Ipswich at the weekend with three tidy finishes, the first two from Rico Lewis assists.

Man City had far too much quality for their Greek visitors despite leaving Erling Haaland in the stands, with Enzo Maresca allowing 17-year-old Floyd Samba to deputise in his place. Maresca proved his point in doing so: City have many other means of scoring beyond Haaland.
Elliot Anderson was also on target in a dominant first half that included 10 efforts on Alberto Brignoli's goal, with Allan striking the crossbar and Rayan Cherki going close.
This was Man City’s 10th win in 12 matches in all competitions this season (L2) – of sides in Europe’s big-five leagues, only Barcelona have won more (11).

articles.title: 'Appalling' batting and 'wickets in clumps' leave England with ODI setback
articles.summary: England captain Harry Brook admits his side were 'too careful' against Pakistan’s spinners after collapsing to a disappointing 87-run defeat in their ODI tri-series opener.
body: Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball in Rawalpindi for the hosts, who recovered from 133-5 to post 302-9 from their 50 overs before skittling England for 215 to claim their second win of the tournament.

Pakistan's all-rounder fired 59 off 58 deliveries and was part of a strong lower middle-order fightback, with Hasan Nawaz top-scoring with a 74-ball 79 and Faheem Ashraf adding 39 off 26 deliveries in the closing overs.

Tom Banton and Ben Duckett shifted the momentum in England's favour with a 91-run opening stand, only for Arafat to bamboozle the visitors with a career-best 6-40 and help Pakistan wrap up victory with more than 11 overs to spare.
"We thought they [Pakistan] were slightly under par," Brook said after their defeat. "It got dewy, as we thought it would do and we were pretty happy at halfway.
